The protocol frames every message with a `Content-Length` header, and the body is arbitrary UTF-8 — a diagnostic message routinely contains newlines, and can contain the blank line that ends a header block. A reader that splits on newlines therefore works on every message anyone writes a test for and fails on real compiler output. It also has to tolerate a pipe delivering one byte at a time, which is why the buffer is kept across calls rather than parsed per chunk; the test feeds it a byte at a time for that reason.

Ported from `orchestrator/runtime/lsp.mjs` (spec 129); the JavaScript this describes is gone.

Written first as two passes — expand the directory wildcard, then rewrite every remaining star — which is wrong, because the second pass rewrites the star inside what the first pass just produced. `src/**/*.c` stopped matching `src/deep.c`, and the test caught it. Reordering the passes would have worked and would have left the trap in place for the next person; matching the tokens in one alternation cannot have the bug at all. An intermediate version parked the wildcard behind a placeholder, which ended up in the file as a literal NUL byte: invisible in a diff, and worse than what it fixed.
